name: David H. Koch Theater
features: Travertine colonnade on Lincoln Center plaza fronts a gilded promenade hall ringed by balconies.

name: Asahi Group Oyamazaki Villa Museum of Art
features: A buried concrete cylinder gallery is reached by a stair from an older English-style hillside villa.
note: Credited to Tadao Ando, who added the underground gallery in 1996; the villa itself was built for Shotaro Kaga.

name: Louvre Museum
note: An institution spanning centuries of building; the key modern work is I. M. Pei's pyramid, a separate entry.

name: Carnegie Hall
features: Renaissance-style brick and terracotta hall with a tiered main auditorium famed for its acoustics.

name: Pushkin Museum of Fine Arts
note: Neoclassical museum of limited design interest for students.

name: Petit Palais
features: Beaux-Arts palace on a trapezoid plan around a semicircular garden court, with top-lit galleries.

name: 40 Wall Street
note: Generic office skyscraper with little design interest for students.

name: 4 World Trade Center
features: Minimal flush glass tower whose parallelogram lower floors become a trapezoid plan higher up.
note: Year corrected to completion (2013).

name: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
features: Venetian-style palazzo of galleries wrapped around a glass-roofed garden courtyard.

name: Kyoto National Museum
features: Brick Meiji-era hall in French baroque style, an early Western-style museum in Japan.
note: Year is the Katayama building's completion (opened 1897).

name: Evolution Tower
features: Two tower strands twist around each other as each floor plate rotates slightly on the one below.

name: Kobe Port Tower
features: Red steel-pipe lattice tower in a hyperboloid hourglass form standing on the harbour.

name: The Index
features: Slim slab tower with service cores at its ends shielding low sun, and shaded long facades.

name: Oscar Niemeyer Museum
features: A raised eye-shaped gallery on a single yellow pier above a pool, beside an earlier long concrete block.

name: 330 North Wabash
features: Dark curtain wall with applied steel I-section mullions above a recessed glass-walled lobby by the river.

name: Haas House
features: Curved glass and stone facade with a projecting cylinder mirrors St Stephen's Cathedral across the square.

name: Jay Pritzker Pavilion
features: Stainless steel ribbons burst around the stage while a steel pipe trellis carries sound over the lawn.

name: Immeuble Clarté
features: Dry-assembled steel-framed flats with full-height glazing, duplexes and glass-block stair landings.

name: Hungerburgbahn stations
features: Double-curved glass shells float over concrete plinths at each funicular station like frozen ice.

name: Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial Library
features: Black steel and glass box over a recessed, fully glazed ground floor with a column-lined loggia.

name: Kyoto Concert Hall
features: A cylindrical entrance hall with a slow spiral ramp leads visitors up to the main concert hall.

name: Brooklyn Museum
note: Unfinished Beaux-Arts museum of limited design interest for this list.

name: Bank of America Tower
features: Faceted crystalline glass tower with angled planes and a spire, planned around green-building systems.

name: Kingdom Centre
features: Tapering tower crowned by an open parabolic arch with a skybridge spanning its top.
note: Year corrected to completion (2002); Omrania added as local architect.

name: Al Janoub Stadium
features: Curved ribbed shell inspired by dhow hulls, with a retractable roof over a cooled seating bowl.

name: Polcevera Viaduct
note: Collapsed in 2018 and was demolished; it no longer stands.

name: State Farm Stadium
features: Ribbed metal and glass skin wraps a bowl with a retractable roof and a pitch that rolls outdoors.

name: Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya
note: Expo palace of limited design interest; year given is not the building's.

name: Radio City Music Hall
by: Edward Durell Stone and Donald Deskey
features: Auditorium ceiling of nested semicircular arches radiates from the stage like a setting sun.

name: One57
features: Cascading curved roofs and two-tone vertically striped glass break down a slender tower.

name: Deutsche Oper Berlin
features: A near-windowless street front of pebble-faced concrete panels over a glazed foyer.

name: Canary Wharf Underground Station
features: Glass canopies pour daylight into a vast concrete hall dug into a former dock.

name: Milwaukee Art Museum, Quadracci Pavilion
features: A winged sunscreen of steel fins opens and folds above a glass reception hall on the lakefront.
note: Year corrected from the museum's founding to Calatrava's pavilion (2001).

name: Pinakothek der Moderne
features: A central rotunda under a glazed dome links four museums along top-lit gallery axes.

name: Tour Duo
features: Two leaning glass towers of different heights share a base beside the railway tracks.

name: Fountain Place
by: Henry N. Cobb (Pei Cobb Freed & Partners)
features: Faceted green-glass prism tower over a Dan Kiley water garden of cypress trees and fountains.

name: Des Moines Art Center
by: Eliel Saarinen, I. M. Pei and Richard Meier
features: Saarinen's low stone wings around a court gain a Pei sculpture wing and a white Meier pavilion.
note: Credit corrected: the 1948 building is by Eliel Saarinen; Pei (1968) and Meier (1985) added wings.

name: San Francisco Federal Building
features: Narrow slab with a perforated steel sunscreen, natural ventilation and skip-stop lifts.

name: OCBC Centre
features: Concrete slab tower whose office floors hang in stacked blocks between two half-cylinder cores.

name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
note: An institution of many buildings by many architects, not one building.

name: Galleria Borghese
note: Year given is the museum's, not the villa's; baroque villa of limited relevance here.

name: 7 World Trade Center
note: Generic office tower with little design interest for students.

name: Natural History Museum, Vienna
by: Gottfried Semper and Carl von Hasenauer
features: Domed neo-Renaissance museum mirroring its twin across a square in Semper's imperial forum plan.

name: Museum of Fine Arts, Budapest
note: Eclectic museum of limited design interest for students.

name: Monument to the Battle of the Nations
features: Massive stepped stone monument over a pool, with a crypt of giant guardians and a domed hall.
note: Credit corrected to architect Bruno Schmitz; Clemens Thieme led the building association.

name: Palau Güell
features: Parabolic-arched gates and a central hall under a perforated dome, topped by mosaic chimneys.

name: One Canada Square
note: Generic office tower with little design interest for students.

name: National Museum of Finland
features: Church-like asymmetric massing and a tall tower blend Finnish medieval and national romantic motifs.
note: Year is the building's completion (opened 1916).

name: The Morgan Library & Museum
features: Marble Renaissance-style library, now joined to its neighbours by Renzo Piano's glass-roofed court.
note: Year corrected from 1924 (museum founding) to the McKim library (1906).

name: Jeu de Paume
note: No usable architect credit and limited design interest.

name: Gare do Oriente
features: Steel and glass canopy of tree-like branching columns shelters raised platforms above the station hall.

name: Sony Center
features: Glass and steel buildings ring an oval forum under a tent-like roof of fabric and glass.
note: Year corrected to the opening (2000).

name: Guggenheim Abu Dhabi
note: Not confirmed as complete; cannot describe the built building truthfully.

name: Tokyo Big Sight
features: Four inverted pyramids raised on legs above a plaza hold the conference halls.
note: Year corrected to the opening (1996).

name: Athens Olympic Stadium roof
features: Two giant tubular steel arches hang a translucent roof over an existing stadium bowl.
note: Credit is Calatrava's 2004 roof; the 1982 stadium is by others, so year changed.

name: United Nations Secretariat Building
by: Wallace K. Harrison with Le Corbusier and Oscar Niemeyer
features: Slab tower with glass curtain-wall long faces and windowless stone-clad ends beside the East River.
note: Credit corrected: Harrison led the design board that included Le Corbusier; year is completion.

name: DR Koncerthuset
features: A blue translucent screen box hides a vineyard-style hall shell, lit with projections at night.

name: Weisman Art Museum
features: Plain brick box to the campus, a cascade of folded stainless steel forms facing the river.
note: Year corrected to Gehry's building (1993).

name: Soreq Nuclear Research Center
features: Battered concrete reactor block fronting a colonnaded courtyard with a long reflecting pool.
note: Year corrected to completion (1960).

name: Cathedral of Saint Mary of the Assumption
by: Pietro Belluschi and Pier Luigi Nervi
features: Four hyperbolic paraboloid concrete shells rise from a square base to meet in a cross of glass.
note: Pietro Belluschi added as design architect with Nervi.

name: National Museum of Ethnology
features: Clustered gallery blocks around a central courtyard, planned to grow in modular units.
note: Year corrected to the building's opening (1977).

name: Kunsten Museum of Modern Art Aalborg
by: Alvar and Elissa Aalto with Jean-Jacques Baruël
features: Roof monitors bounce daylight off curved reflectors into white galleries set in a wooded hollow.

name: Wangjing SOHO
features: Three mountain-like towers wrapped in continuous flowing bands of white aluminium and glass.

name: Binoculars Building
by: Frank Gehry with Claes Oldenburg and Coosje van Bruggen
features: Giant binoculars form the car entrance between a ship-like white wing and a copper tree-like wing.

name: Beppu B-Con Plaza
note: Not known well enough to describe truthfully.

name: Trump Tower
note: Generic commercial tower with little design interest.

name: International Commerce Centre
note: Generic commercial tower with little design interest.

name: Peace Palace
note: Neo-Renaissance palace of limited interest; year given was the start of building (finished 1913).

name: Bargello
note: Medieval palace; year given is the museum's opening and the building's credit is uncertain.

name: Scottish National Gallery
note: Neoclassical gallery of limited design interest for this list.

name: Flame Towers
features: Three flame-shaped glass towers whose LED-covered facades show moving flames at night.

name: New Town Hall, Munich
features: Long neo-Gothic facade on Marienplatz with a tall tower holding a mechanical Glockenspiel.

name: Philadelphia City Hall
features: Load-bearing masonry block around a central court, its tower crowned by a statue of William Penn.

name: Hamburger Bahnhof
features: A former railway terminus turned gallery, its iron-and-glass train hall kept as the main space.

name: Westendstrasse 1
note: Generic office tower with little design interest.

name: Norton Simon Museum
note: Credit wrong: the building is by Ladd & Kelsey (1969); Gehry only remodelled galleries in 1999.

name: Miami Tower
note: Generic commercial tower with little design interest.

name: Saint Louis Art Museum, East Building
features: Low pavilion of dark polished concrete with a deep coffered ceiling that admits daylight.
note: Credit changed to Chipperfield's 2013 wing; the 1904 Cass Gilbert building is the older part.

name: Villa Le Lac
features: A long low lakeside house with one strip window and a garden wall pierced to frame the lake.

name: Tour EDF (Tour Légende)
note: Generic office tower; not known well enough to describe truthfully.
